paragraphs: Vibelly is only for people aged 18 or older. You confirm you are 18+ before every chat. This is a self-declaration: Vibelly does not check ID. If you are under 18, do not use Vibelly. Signed-in accounts found to belong to minors are banned.

bullets: No nudity, sexual content, or sexual requests.
No harassment, hate speech, threats, or bullying.
No spam, scams, advertising, or links to other services.
No recording or screenshotting people without their consent.
No illegal activity of any kind.

paragraphs: You can start a video or text chat without creating an account. Reporting someone requires you to be signed in, so that reports are tied to real accounts and cannot be abused anonymously.

Every call has a Report button. Reports are reviewed by hand, and signed-in accounts that break these rules are banned; serious cases lead to a permanent ban. Only signed-in users can be reported and banned. Someone chatting as a guest has no account to report, so if a guest breaks the rules, skip them: skipping ends the call instantly.
You can also email reports to vibellyofficial@gmail.com with the time of the call and what happened.

Video and voice calls connect directly between browsers using WebRTC, which encrypts media in transit. When a direct connection is not possible, media passes through a relay server, which forwards it without being able to read it. As with any peer-to-peer video call, the other person can see your IP address, which can reveal your approximate location.

Vibelly does not record calls, and random chat messages are not stored. A basic record of each random call (the two participants, call type, video quality and length) is kept for 24 hours to help with abuse reports, then deleted automatically. Direct messages between signed-in users are kept for up to 24 hours (the last 25 per conversation) so you can read them, then deleted.

If you sign in, we store your account details, your Premium status, and the details of any reports you make or receive, so that we can enforce these rules. If you use groups, live streams, or a creator profile, we also store what those features need; the Terms & Privacy Policy lists it all.

bullets: Never share your full name, address, school, workplace, or financial details.
Skip any conversation instantly. You never owe a stranger your time.
Be careful with requests to move to another app. That is a common scam pattern.
Assume anything you show on camera could be recorded by the other person.
If someone threatens or blackmails you, do not pay. Keep evidence, report the account, and contact your local police.

If someone threatens to share intimate images of you, StopNCII.org (adults) and Take It Down (takeitdown.ncmec.org, for images taken when you were under 18) can help stop them spreading. In India, report online crimes at cybercrime.gov.in or call the 1930 helpline.

sections.h2: Why people look for a Chatroulette alternative
paragraphs: Chatroulette launched in November 2009 and is still running. Most people looking for an alternative want one of three things: a different crowd, a site that works without an app, or stricter rules about who can join.

Age checks are the hard part for every service. An October 2025 [LBC investigation](https://www.lbc.co.uk/news/exclusive/video-chatrooms-british-children/) reported that Chatroulette did not require proof of age. Vibelly does not check ID either: you confirm you are 18 or older before every chat, and signed-in accounts found to belong to minors are banned. If proof of age matters to you, note that none of the services we compared state that they verify ID.

sections.h2: How random video chat works on Vibelly
paragraphs: Random video chat pairs you with a stranger for a live, one-to-one video call. On Vibelly, you open the site, confirm you are 18 or older, allow camera and microphone access, and press start. A matching server pairs you with someone who is waiting, then gets out of the way.

The call itself connects directly between the two browsers using WebRTC, which encrypts audio and video in transit. When a direct connection is not possible, a relay server forwards the call without being able to read it. Calls are never recorded.
You can skip to someone new at any time. Free video runs at 480p and adapts to your connection; Premium adds 720p HD, voice-only calls, and gender and country filters.
Ready to try it? Start a chat from the Vibelly homepage.

sections.h2: What to expect on your first random video call
paragraphs: Your browser asks for camera and microphone access the first time. Allow both, check that your face is lit and your background shows nothing personal, then confirm you are 18 or older.
Matching usually takes a few seconds, longer at quiet times because Vibelly is still a small community. When the call connects you will see the other person straight away, and they will see you.

Many first calls are short. People skip quickly while they look for someone to talk to, so do not take it personally, and feel free to do the same. Free video runs at 480p and adapts to your connection; if the picture is choppy, a steadier Wi-Fi signal helps more than anything else.

If anything makes you uncomfortable, skip at once. If you are signed in, you can also report the other person, as long as they are signed in too; every report is reviewed by hand. Our [random video chat safety checklist](/blog/random-video-chat-safety-checklist) covers the rest.

bullets: "Where are you calling from?" Easy to answer, and it leads somewhere.
"What is the time where you are?" A natural follow-up that often turns into a story.
"What is something you are into that most people do not know about?"
"What food from your country should I try?"
Notice something real: a poster, a guitar, a view. It shows you are paying attention.
paragraphs: After they answer, share something of your own so it feels like a conversation, not an interview. If the chat is not clicking, say "nice talking to you" and skip. Our guide How to Start a Conversation With a Stranger has more ideas.

sections.h2: What if the conversation goes quiet?
bullets: Silence is normal in the first few seconds. Give the other person a moment to set up their camera before you skip.
Fall back on what you can see: their background, the time of day where they are, the language on a sign behind them.
Ask a follow-up instead of a new question. "What made you pick that?" keeps a thread going.
If you want to practise a language, say so early. Many people are happy to switch, and our guide to [practising a language on video chat](/blog/practice-a-language-on-video-chat) has more ideas.

sections.h2: When to skip, and when to report
bullets: Skip whenever a conversation is not working for you. Skipping is never penalised.
Report signed-in users who are sexual, abusive, hateful, or appear to be under 18. Reporting requires signing in, every report is reviewed by hand, and guests cannot be reported, so skip them.
Be wary of anyone who quickly asks you to move to another app or asks for money, codes, or photos. Those are common scam patterns.
Remember the other person can see your IP address on a peer-to-peer call, so never share your full name, address, school, or workplace.

sections.h2: Talking to strangers when you are shy
bullets: Start with text chat. You can switch to video once you feel comfortable, or never.
Keep three questions ready before you press start, so the first ten seconds are covered.
Set a small goal, such as one conversation that lasts two minutes. It is easier to begin than to aim for a great chat.
Treat a skip as information, not rejection. People skip for all sorts of reasons, including their own nerves.
End on your terms. "Nice talking to you, good luck with the exam" is a complete goodbye.

paragraphs: Talking to strangers is a low-pressure way to practise conversation. Nobody you know is watching, and if a chat does not go well you can simply move on. People use random chat to beat boredom, to hear how life looks in another country, to practise a language with native speakers, or just to have a conversation they could never have predicted.

Research backs this up. In a study of Chicago commuters, people asked to talk to a stranger reported a more pleasant journey than people asked to keep to themselves, even though most predicted the opposite ([Epley & Schroeder, 2014](https://doi.org/10.1037/a0037323)). Another study found people felt happier on days when they talked with more casual acquaintances, not just close friends ([Sandstrom & Dunn, 2014](https://doi.org/10.1177/0146167214529799)). Both studies looked at face-to-face conversations, not video chat, but the lesson carries over: a short chat with someone new tends to go better than you expect.

It also tends to go better than it feels. Researchers found that after a first conversation, people consistently underestimate how much the other person liked them, which they call the "liking gap" ([Boothby et al., 2018](https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797618783714)). If a chat felt awkward to you, it probably felt fine to them.
On Vibelly you can start a free video or text chat in your browser, with no app to install. You confirm you are 18 or older before every chat, and you can skip to someone new at any time.

sections.h2: What anonymous chat means on Vibelly
paragraphs: Anonymous chat on Vibelly means you can start a random video or text chat without creating an account, giving an email address, or sharing a phone number. You are matched with a stranger, and neither of you sees a profile, a name, or a follower count unless you choose to share it.

It does not mean invisible. On any peer-to-peer video call, the other person's browser can see your IP address, which can reveal your approximate location. The other person can also record their own screen, so assume anything you show on camera could be saved. Choose a plain background and keep identifying details off camera.

Some features need an account: Vibelly Premium, direct messages, and reporting. Reporting requires signing in with Google or GitHub, so reports are tied to real accounts. Signing in does not show your name or email to the people you chat with.

sections.h2: What is and is not stored
bullets: Random chats: video and voice connect directly between browsers, encrypted in transit, and are never recorded. Random text chat messages are relayed and not stored. A basic record of each random call (the two participants, call type, video quality and length) is kept for 24 hours to help with abuse reports, then deleted automatically.
If you sign in: your name, username, email, and profile image from Google or GitHub, the gender and country you choose, your Premium status, and any reports you make or receive.
Direct messages between signed-in users: the last 25 per conversation are kept for up to 24 hours, then deleted.
Payments are handled by Razorpay. Vibelly never receives your card details.
Your IP address is visible to the other person during a peer-to-peer call.
paragraphs: Full details are in the Terms & Privacy Policy.

sections.h2: Downsides of anonymous chat, and how to reduce them
bullets: People can behave worse when nobody knows who they are. Psychologists call this the [online disinhibition effect](https://doi.org/10.1089/1094931041291295). Skip anyone who turns rude or sexual; skipping ends the call instantly.
You cannot verify who you are talking to. On Vibelly, as on every site in this category, age is self-declared, and the other person's name and story may not be true.
Guests cannot be reported on Vibelly, because there is no account to act on. Only signed-in users can be reported and banned, so skip a guest who breaks the rules.
Anonymous does not mean invisible. The other person can see your IP address on a peer-to-peer call and can record their own screen.
Scammers use anonymity too. Be wary of anyone who asks you to move to another app or to send money, codes, or photos.
Use a first name or nickname only.
Keep your school, workplace, street, and social media handles to yourself.
Be careful with requests to move to another app, or to send photos, money, or codes.
Skip any conversation that makes you uncomfortable, and report signed-in users who break the rules.

sections.h2: How do I report a user by email?
bullets: The date and approximate time of the call, with your time zone.
Whether it was a video, voice, or text chat.
What happened, in a sentence or two.
A screenshot if you have one. Never send images that show nudity or a minor: describe them instead.
If you were signed in, the email address on your account, so we can find the call.

sections.h2: What if I am in danger?
paragraphs: If someone threatens you or a child is at risk, contact your local police first. In India you can also report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930. Vibelly does not record calls, so the details you give us are what we have to act on.
